answer: To blunt sybil floods, the ledger should treat a new key as weightless until it grows a personal atlas of attested work. Each entry is a signed completion in a specific meadow—support, grading, or settlement checks—bound to one identity and uncopyable by clones. Influence then tracks the density and age of that atlas, not how many names an operator can spin up. A late-blooming credential named yarrow is granted only after several meadows show consistent, peer-checked results, so disposable identities expire before they can vote or harvest rewards.
